1. All non-negative: $n_1 > n_2 > \dots > n_r \ge 0$
2. All negative: $0 > n_1 > n_2 > \dots > n_r$
3. Mixed signs: $n_1 > \dots > n_i \ge 0 > n_{i+1} > \dots > n_r$ for $1 \le i \le r-1$.

For the mixed sign regions, the multiple sum factors exactly into a product of a depth $i$ sum and a depth $r-i$ sum. Since both depths are strictly less than $r$, these intermediate regions are completely discarded when working modulo products of lower depth. Hence, we are left with the sum over the all-positive region and the all-negative region summing to $0$ modulo products:
$$ \sum_{n_1 > \dots > n_r \ge 0} + \sum_{0 > n_1 > \dots > n_r} \equiv 0 \pmod{\text{products}} $$

$$ m_1 > m_2 > \dots > m_r \ge 0 $$

$$ (n_i+a)^{k_i} = (-m_{r+1-i} - 1 + a)^{k_i} = (-1)^{k_i} (m_{r+1-i} + 1 - a)^{k_i} $$
Taking the product over $i=1, \dots, r$, the sign becomes $(-1)^{k_1+\dots+k_r}$. Reindexing the product with $j = r+1-i$ flips the sequence of the powers $k_i$ to $k_{r+1-j}$.
